🧠 Crypto News Brief: Crypto is stuck in regulatory limbo. Bitcoin hovers near $63K as ETF outflows return, Washington's rulebook stalls at both the SEC and Senate, and fresh exploits keep the security spotlight burning — leaving markets coiled and waiting for a catalyst. 📉 Bitcoin Pinned Near $63K as Spot ETFs Log First Two-Day August Outflow Bitcoin drifted around $63,000 in thin weekend trade after a softer-than-feared July inflation print failed to spark a rally. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs booked back-to-back redemptions — August's first two-day outflow streak, roughly $187M pulled — while Ether tracked sideways near $1,880 and the market coiled for a volatility expansion. Read full story → 🏛️ SEC Abruptly Pulls Its First-Ever 'Regulation Crypto' Vote The SEC cancelled its August 14 open meeting — what would have been the first crypto-specific rulemaking in the agency's history — citing an unforeseen scheduling issue and setting no new date. The shelved proposal would have opened a tailored fundraising pathway for token projects, leaving issuers stuck with existing registration routes. More details → ⚖️ Galaxy Slashes CLARITY Act Odds to 10% as Senate Vote Slips to September Galaxy Research cut its estimate for the crypto market-structure bill passing in 2026 to just 10%, down from 60% in spring, warning the Senate has only two-to-three weeks after returning September 14 and unresolved fights over ethics rules and stablecoin yield. A cloture vote is set for September 15. Read more → 🔓 Weekly Crypto Losses Top $37M as $25.6M Whale Phishing Strikes Again Researchers logged more than $37M in confirmed losses over the week, led by a repeat $25.6M phishing drain of a single whale, a $7.9M Coinsbuy breach and several cross-chain mint exploits — all stacking on top of the Coldcard firmware fallout, whose stolen bitcoin cache has now climbed past $130M. See details → 🏦 RedotPay Shelves $1B U.S. IPO to 2027 Amid $470M Binance Lawsuit Stablecoin payments firm RedotPay postponed its planned $1B U.S. listing — now unlikely before 2027 — as it works through regulatory approvals and a $470M Binance lawsuit alleging it poached roughly 470,000 users. The company said it just secured a U.S. money transmitter license and is preparing a stateside launch. 77557.subject: Weekly Recap: Trust, Don't Verify
77557.body:
**gm, Defiers!**

**Tether** cleared the first full audit in its 12-year history this week, then published neither the statements nor the opinion letter.

The pattern repeated all week. **Robinhood Chain**'s first NFT sellout moved 44,444 tokens in under an hour through a contract Blockscout still lists as unverified. **ENS** tokenholders handed a $65 million endowment to a foundation whose spending limits, a co-founder pointed out, exist in the proposal's prose and nowhere in the executable. And Bitcoin's BIP editors removed **Luke Dashjr** from the repository two days after his fork stalled, by a process BIP 3 does not describe.

In Washington, SEC staff cleared **Franklin Templeton** to use its onchain money fund as collateral inside registered funds. The price of admission was 12 conditions and a transfer agent that can freeze any wallet.

Enjoy!

———————————————————————————

———————————————————————————

———————————————————————————

##### WATCH

## Inside Bitcoin's Worst Security Stretch in Years

Youtube: 🟢 LIVE: Inside Bitcoin's Worst Security Stretch in Years w/ Foundation & Casa CEOs (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eFBSwG65emE)

Camila Russo talks to **Foundation** CEO **Zach Herbert**, whose Lightning node was swept in the BTCPay Server attack, and **Casa** CEO **Nick Neuman** about three weeks that ran from a 2021 Coldcard firmware bug through Boltz shutting down to merchant nodes being drained overnight.

———————————————————————————

# Top Stories This Week

## Tether Clears Its First Full Audit and Publishes None of It

**KPMG US** issued an unqualified opinion on the 2025 accounts of Tether International, S.A. de C.V., the El Salvador entity that issues USDT, [the first full financial-statement audit in the company's history](https://thedefiant.io/news/cefi/tether-clears-first-full-audit-from-kpmg-without-publishing-the-statements). The work was performed to **AICPA** standards; the GENIUS Act sets **PCAOB** standards for licensed US issuers. Tether has released neither the statements nor the opinion letter, so the audit's existence is the only fact in evidence. A full audit was the longest-running demand on the company, and Tether met it on the softer standard with the documents withheld.

## Robinhood Chain Built Almost All of Crypto's Launchpad Growth

Launchpads collected $75.39 million in fees over the 30 days to Aug. 11, against $42.53 million the month before, and [Robinhood Chain produced $33.49 million of it](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/pump-fun-launchpad-fee-share-falls-robinhood-chain-pons-noxa), up 236% from its own first month. **Pump.fun**'s share of the category fell to 26.7% in the week to July 14, then recovered above half four weeks later on its largest weekly haul in 90 days. The chain also took its first NFT sellout: ousted **Pudgy Penguins** co-founder **Cole Villemain** [moved 44,444 Spritehood tokens in 54 minutes](https://thedefiant.io/news/nfts-and-web3/ousted-pudgy-penguins-co-founder-sells-out-44-444-p
